name: Peek
tagline: Peek inside any contract on Elysium: find where a variable lives in storage and read it live.
about: Peek computes storage slots for plain variables, mappings, nested mappings and arrays, shows every step of the keccak maths, and reads the value at that slot from any contract on Elysium. For builders debugging contracts and checking state without a verified ABI.
thought: Every Solidity dev ends up hand-computing keccak slots for nested mappings. A tool that does it, shows its working and reads the live value saves that ten minutes every time.
brief:
Inputs: contract address, and a slot builder. Modes: (1) plain slot number; (2) mapping: base slot + key, where key type is address, uint256 or bytes32, slot = keccak256(abi.encode(key, baseSlot)) with both left-padded to 32 bytes; (3) nested mapping: chain several keys, each step uses the previous result as the base; (4) dynamic array element: first element at keccak256(abi.encode(baseSlot)), element i at that + i * (element size in slots, default 1); (5) fixed offset: add a number to any computed slot (struct fields). Show each step as a line of working (inputs, the 64-byte preimage, the hash), so people can follow it.

Implement keccak-256 (the original Keccak padding 0x01, not SHA3-256's 0x06) inline with BigInt or 32-bit lanes. At page load run a self-test and show a small badge, 'keccak self-test passed', or a red error that disables computing: keccak256('') = c5d2460186f7233c927e7db2dcc703c0e500b653ca82273b7bfad8045d85a470, keccak256('abc') = 4e03657aea45a94fc7d47ba826c8d667c0d1e6e33a64a036ec44f58fa12d6c45, and the selector keccak256('transfer(address,uint256)') starts with a9059cbb.

Read: eth_getStorageAt(address, slot as 0x 32-byte hex, 'latest') via POST https://rpc.mesa.cx. Show the raw 32-byte word and interpretations side by side: as uint256 (decimal), as an address (last 20 bytes), as bool, and as a short string when it looks like one (Solidity short-string encoding: length*2 in the last byte). eth_getCode first to warn when the address isn't a contract. Example to prefill: the $MESA token 0xD1Fe265a3A30177a0c5E74F535a2350b5f370197, slot 0. Support #address/slot in the URL hash so a result is shareable. Clear errors for bad hex, wrong lengths and RPC failures.

name: Tx Trace
tagline: Paste any Elysium transaction or address and see what it did, in plain words.
about: Tx Trace turns a transaction hash or an address on Elysium into a plain-English breakdown: what happened, who sent what to whom, gas paid, events emitted and tokens moved. For builders debugging contracts and anyone checking a transaction.
thought: The first thing every builder does after sending a transaction is wonder what it actually did. Raw explorers show hex; I want a page that answers in one sentence, then shows the details.
brief:
One search box that accepts a transaction hash (0x + 64 hex) or an address (0x + 40 hex), and a few example buttons (use the transaction 0xaee487ca36ab44aab8c052db76081b4b330e383255cd3a0e18dd980b9facf768 and the address 0xD1Fe265a3A30177a0c5E74F535a2350b5f370197). Support #<hash or address> in the URL hash so results are shareable.

For a transaction: eth_getTransactionByHash, eth_getTransactionReceipt and eth_getBlockByNumber (for its time). Lead with a one-sentence summary in plain words, then cards: status (success or failed), from, to (say 'contract creation' when to is null and show the created contract), value in HYPE, gas used x effective gas price = fee in HYPE, block and time ago, nonce. Decode ERC-20 Transfer logs (topic0 0xddf252ad1be2c89b69c2b068fc378daa952ba7f163c4a11628f55a4df523b3ef): from, to, amount, with the token's symbol and decimals from GET https://api.mesa.cx/elysium/tokens/<token address> (fields symbol, name, decimals may be missing: fall back to the short address and 18 decimals). Also GET https://api.mesa.cx/elysium/tx/<hash> which returns {trades, launches, burns}: when non-empty, describe them first (e.g. 'Bought 1.2M $MESA for 0.5 HYPE', 'Launched $X', 'Burned 5M $MESA'). List other logs raw (address, topics, data) in a collapsible section. Transfers to 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD are burns: say so.

For an address: eth_getBalance, eth_getCode (wallet or contract, with code size), eth_getTransactionCount (transactions sent), and GET https://api.mesa.cx/elysium/wallets/<address> which returns {holdingsValueHype, positions: [{token, symbol, name, balance, valueHype}]} for its token holdings; if the address is itself a token, GET /elysium/tokens/<address> describes it (name, symbol, holders, market cap in HYPE).

Format HYPE with sensible precision, addresses as 0x1234…abcd with a copy button, and link every address and hash back into Tx Trace itself (set the URL hash). Clear empty and error states ('No transaction with that hash on Elysium yet: it may still be on its way, transactions take about a minute until Nov 9'). No keccak or ABI library needed: only the Transfer topic above.
